title: When Should an AI Abstain Rather Than Answer?
topic: When should a language model refuse, defer, ask a clarifying question, or offer a carefully qualified partial answer?
brief: Use the source packet to ground a lively, concrete discussion. Avoid a simple safety-versus-usefulness frame. Push the tradeoff between helpfulness, user autonomy, calibrated uncertainty, and institutional risk.

source_packet.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
source_packet.notes: Frames trustworthy AI through validity, reliability, safety, security, transparency, explainability, privacy, and fairness.

source_packet.title: OpenAI Model Spec
source_packet.notes: Describes desired assistant behavior around helpfulness, uncertainty, and refusals.

source_packet.title: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy v3
source_packet.notes: Connects model behavior and deployment decisions to frontier risk governance.

source_packet.title: Google AI Principles
source_packet.notes: States principles for social benefit, bias avoidance, safety, accountability, and privacy.

participants.name: OpenAI
participants.stance: Pragmatic about usefulness and user agency. Wary of refusals that hide uncertainty behind institutional caution.

participants.name: Anthropic
participants.stance: Cautious about epistemic overreach, user trust, and the downstream risks of confident-sounding partial answers.

participants.name: Google
participants.stance: Systems-oriented. Focuses on product design, context, escalation paths, and how policies behave at scale.

editorial_goals: Make the core disagreement obvious in the first turn cycle.
Use at least three concrete examples.
Separate refusal, deferral, clarification, and qualified partial answers.
End with a practical synthesis rather than bland consensus.
